headline: Large User Grid Cost Shift
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of grid infrastructure for large energy users, such as data centers, away from residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling.
opponents: Large energy users, data center industry, some critics of Governor's amendments.
news_headline: Governor Amends Data Center Cost Shift Bills
news_summary: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393, a measure designed to shift more energy costs onto data centers and large manufacturers to save residential electricity customers money. Critics argue that the governor's amendments, which removed a direct cost shift for purchasing additional power through PJM, weakened the bill's original intent to protect ratepayers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates data centers to report their water consumption, increasing transparency regarding their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups (e.g., Potomac Conservancy, Piedmont Environmental Council), local communities, transparency advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (may view as administrative burden).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the information publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This legislation aims to address concerns about the significant water consumption by the rapidly growing data center industry in Virginia.

headline: Data Center Siting & Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill establishes new regulations for data center siting, requiring site assessments for noise and other environmental impacts, and allowing localities to impose noise limits.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near potential data center sites, environmental groups (e.g., Piedmont Environmental Council, Virginia Conservation Network), Delegate Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry (may face increased regulatory hurdles and costs).
news_headline: Data Center Reform Legislation Addresses Siting, Noise
news_summary: HB 153, supported by the Virginia Conservation Network, requires data centers to provide localities with noise impact assessments on nearby residential areas and schools. It also allows localities to require site assessments for impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forests, giving local governments more tools to manage data center development.
